projects.title: Seating Chart
projects.summary: Plan classroom layouts and randomize seats with attendance, groups, and placement constraints.
projects.overview: A browser-based classroom planning tool with separate classes, reusable layouts, and table or grid seating. Student lists and layouts are saved in this browser on the website’s origin.
features: Manage multiple classes, student sublists, and attendance.
Create, name, color, move, and resize tables with one to eight seats.
Configure grid rows, columns, spacing, and aisles.
Randomize seating with seat locks, table locks, and student separation constraints.
Save shared layouts and use fullscreen classroom presentation.
usage: Open the tool and choose or create a class.
Paste names one per line, then configure tables or a grid.
Set attendance and placement options before randomizing seats.
notes: Saved data stays in the browser where it was created. A different browser or domain has separate data.
The existing tool opens at its original URL; this showcase does not read or write classroom data.

projects.title: Hex Math
projects.summary: Change one multiplication factor, claim a product, and connect four hexes in a two-player game.
projects.overview: A local two-player multiplication strategy game. Players change one factor at a time; the matching product is claimed automatically when it is available.
features: Choose factors from 1 through 12.
Alternate turns on a shuffled board of multiplication products.
Connect four owned hexes along a board axis to win.
Track wins during the current page session and start a new board.
usage: Share the screen with another player.
Select a different value in either factor panel; the game claims the matching unclaimed product.
Use New game or Play again to start another board.

preview.alt: Hex Math interface with player scores, factor controls, and a board of multiplication products.
preview.caption: Screenshot of the existing browser game, captured locally without changing its rules.

projects.title: Sort the Numbers
projects.summary: Select shuffled numbers from one to five in ascending order.
projects.overview: A small browser game built around a simple sequence challenge: find the shuffled numbers and click them in order from one to five.
features: Shuffle five numbered cards at the start of each round.
Mark correct selections as you progress.
Restart automatically after success or an incorrect selection.
usage: Dismiss the result message to continue with a freshly shuffled round.
notes: The original game uses mouse-clickable cards and browser alerts. Its interactions are preserved in this milestone.

preview.alt: Sort the Numbers interface showing five shuffled numbered cards.
preview.caption: Screenshot of the existing browser game, captured locally without changing its rules.

projects.title: Auto Clicker
projects.summary: A Python desktop utility with configurable click intervals, mouse buttons, and a start/stop hotkey.
projects.overview: A desktop auto-clicking project described in the development Blog. Its interface lets users configure repeated mouse clicks and a global hotkey.
features: Configure the interval between clicks.
Choose the mouse button to use.
Customize the start/stop hotkey, with F4 described as the default.
Run clicking on a separate thread so the interface remains responsive.
notes: This is desktop software, not an application that runs inside this website.
The source repository is available. No separate executable download is advertised here.

preview.alt: Auto Clicker desktop window with interval, mouse-button, and hotkey controls.
preview.caption: Existing project screenshot from the development Blog.

projects.title: Vacation Planner
projects.summary: A mobile vacation-planning application presented as a WGU capstone project.
projects.overview: A mobile application introduced in the Blog as the WGU capstone project. The original post provides an APK through Google Drive.
features: Vacation-planning mobile application.
APK shared through the existing Google Drive destination.
usage: Open the Google Drive destination to find Capstone.apk and its Download control.
notes: The download destination was checked and displays Capstone.apk. The APK was not installed or tested.
The repository does not include the mobile app’s source or screenshots, so no framework or additional features are claimed.

projects.title: Hotdog Counter
projects.summary: A mobile application represented here by its published privacy policy.
projects.overview: The website hosts the privacy policy for the Hotdog Counter mobile application. The policy is the verified project material available in this repository.
features: Published privacy policy with an application data-use statement.
Contact email provided in the policy.
notes: No application download, live demo, source repository, or screenshots are linked in the available project material.
The original policy URL and its content remain unchanged.

projects.title: Tennessee City Guide
projects.summary: Explore a five-page Tennessee website featuring Nashville, Knoxville, Chattanooga, and a contact-form example.
projects.overview: A preserved coursework website introducing Tennessee and three of its cities. It includes illustrated state facts, city statistics, and links to weather, maps, and local government information.
features: State overview and illustrated facts.
Dedicated Nashville, Knoxville, and Chattanooga pages.
City weather, map, and government links.
Contact-form demonstration with matching-email validation.
usage: Open the coursework and use its own menu to explore the state, cities, and form.
notes: The application’s original orange design and internal navigation are preserved.
The contact form is a coursework demonstration; it has no message-delivery backend.

preview.alt: Tennessee map illustration used on the original coursework homepage.
preview.caption: Original Tennessee coursework illustration; not a screenshot of the dashboard.

projects.title: Feedback Survey Demo
projects.summary: A client-side feedback form demonstrating required-answer validation and a thank-you message.
projects.overview: A browser form example with text, selection, radio, checkbox, and optional comment fields. Its JavaScript validates required answers before showing a personalized acknowledgment.
features: Multiple input types and required-answer validation.
Inline validation messages.
Personalized thank-you state after valid answers.
notes: This is a form demonstration. It does not transmit, email, or store submitted answers.

projects.title: Bootstrap Cover Page
projects.summary: An earlier portfolio About page preserved from an internet software course.
projects.overview: A legacy About page built from the Bootstrap cover example for an internet software class. It preserves an earlier biography, portrait, and template attribution.
features: Bootstrap cover layout and responsive utilities.
Profile image and original student biography.
Original template attribution and navigation.
notes: This historical page is retained at its existing URL. Its biography describes the time when it was created.

projects.title: ChrisWellsDev Website
projects.summary: A static developer portfolio bringing together interactive tools, games, software, and coursework.
projects.overview: This website brings together browser applications, software project notes, and coursework in a shared developer dashboard design. Static HTML keeps its core navigation and project links available without JavaScript.
features: A categorized project catalog and dedicated Tools & Games page.
Consistent showcase layouts, cards, and responsive navigation.
Direct links to the original interactive tools.
Static hosting through GitHub Pages.
notes: No runtime framework, backend, or build step is required to serve the checked-in pages.
